formulas: Contribution for a period = earned customer revenue less provider compensation, employer burden, variable delivery costs and allocated variable operating effort. This is not net profit.

remaining_discovery_questions: Which state, school district type and initial discipline are in scope: SLP only, or a bundled SLP/OT/PT service?
Are we supplying staff under district direction, contracting to deliver defined therapy services, or both? Who retains service-record and clinical-supervision responsibility?
Which roles approve requisitions, budgets, candidates, onboarding, schedules, documentation, time and invoices? Obtain the current signed agreement, SOW, amendments and order form.
Which existing district systems own student records, service schedules, therapist attendance, Medicaid support and accounts payable? What permitted API, export or manual evidence channels exist?
What direct/indirect workload, travel, meetings and supervision must fit into each provider's contracted time? What constitutes an accepted workload change?
How do provider absence, student absence, school closure, testing schedules, technology failure and planned leave each affect service recovery, customer billing and worker pay?
Who decides whether missed services require recovery, which plan is approved and when an exception can be closed?
Are assistants and clinical fellows permitted, under what supervision, and can a replacement change qualification level?
When is virtual delivery allowed, who chooses the platform, and what school-side facilitator, room, device and accessibility support is required?
Which student-linked data are actually necessary in the staffing system, who may see them, and what approved retention/deletion rules apply?
How are invoice disputes, after-submission corrections and actual cash receipt measured? What is the complete payment trigger, not just the stated number of days?
Which three recurring exceptions consume the most staff time, and what evidence would let an agent safely prepare the next action?

Show the blank forms and approval chain for a new order, candidate, schedule and assignment extension.
Which services and administrative duties are included in the requested hours, and who checks that the workload fits?
Which systems must a supplier use? Where do staff currently re-enter the same information?
Walk through one provider absence, one student absence and one closure. Who makes the recovery and billing decisions?
What evidence makes a timecard and invoice acceptable? What causes rejection or delayed payment?
Which actions could a staffing agent execute under a preapproved rule, and which require a named person's decision?
artifacts_to_request: De-identified exception categories and timing counts

interview_guides.audience: School SLP, plus OT/PT comparison participants if those disciplines enter scope
interview_guides.format: Proposed 45 minute day-in-the-life walkthrough; no student identities or clinical narratives collected.
questions: Map a normal week across direct service, evaluation, documentation, meetings, consultation and travel.
What information must you receive before accepting an assignment? Which surprises make an assignment unworkable?
Where do you record work time versus service delivery? What gets entered twice?
What happens when a session is missed or only partly delivered? Which decisions require your judgment?
Which reminders, prefilled administrative forms or reconciliation checks would save time without creating extra review?
How do you obtain support for access problems, room/equipment issues, workload changes and payroll corrections?
For virtual work, what happens at the school end before a session can start, and how are outages recorded?

interview_guides.format: Proposed 60 minute end-to-end tabletop using one synthetic SLP placement; no outreach performed.

Where are district-specific rules stored, who updates them, and how do amendments reach payroll and billing?
What handoff makes a selected candidate ready to start? What is still unresolved after the client says yes?
How do you replace a provider while preserving access, qualification, supervision and continuity requirements?
How do time, documentation and invoice exceptions get reconciled without delaying unrelated obligations?
What cannot currently be observed through APIs or exports, and who can authorize an approved integration?
Show the evidence needed to reverse an incorrect agent action and identify who owns the recovery.

research_limits: No jurisdiction or real district is selected; numerical clauses are examples rather than adopted pilot defaults.

obligations.title: School therapy staffing: obligations research matrix
obligations.status: Source-grounded requirements research; proposed system behavior; jurisdiction and district rules unresolved

scope.worked_example: Speech-language pathologist (SLP), with occupational therapy (OT) and physical therapy (PT) distinctions
scope.geography: United States; state and school district not selected
scope.setting_assumption: K–12 public-school IDEA Part B services for the worked example; verify applicability for each client
exclusions: No real student or worker records queried
No independent clinical diagnosis or IEP decision by AI
No universal caseload, service-minute, clearance, or retention rule inferred
scope.interpretation: Official sources establish research principles. The software behaviors and acceptance tests below are proposed controls, not findings about Amergis systems or a completed legal determination.

sources.title: IDEA §300.34 — Related services
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved
sources.supports: Speech-language pathology, occupational therapy and physical therapy are identified related services. OT and PT are services supplied by qualified practitioners; discipline-specific functions differ.
sources.limit: Does not establish the qualifications or scope for a selected state, school or individual.

sources.title: IDEA §300.156(b) — Related services personnel and paraprofessionals
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed subsection text retrieved; parent section direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: Qualifications must align with applicable state-recognized discipline requirements. Related-services requirements cannot be waived on an emergency, temporary or provisional basis. Appropriately trained and supervised assistants may assist in accordance with state law, regulation or written policy.
sources.limit: Does not make a national association credential, professional license and school credential interchangeable.

sources.title: IDEA §300.320(a) — IEP content
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed subsection text retrieved; parent section direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: An IEP includes goals, progress measurement/reporting, services and projected start, frequency, location and duration.
sources.limit: Provides no universal therapy minutes or caseload. The individual authorized plan supplies service obligations.

sources.title: IDEA §300.323(d) — IEP access and implementation responsibilities
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official subsection and official CFR text retrieved through search; parent section direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: Responsible providers must have access to the IEP and be informed of their implementation responsibilities and required accommodations, modifications and supports.
sources.limit: Does not prescribe a vendor's data model or make a schedule equivalent to delivered service.

sources.title: FERPA regulations — 34 CFR Part 99
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, Student Privacy Policy Office
sources.evidence_status: Official full page retrieved
sources.supports: Covered schools need consent or an applicable disclosure exception. Outsourced school officials require an institutional function, school control, permitted use/redisclosure and legitimate educational interest. Parents and eligible students have access/amendment rights; pending inspection requests restrict destruction.
sources.limit: A staffing contract alone does not establish the exception; schools and record types differ. Technical logging proposed here is broader than any universal FERPA disclosure-log requirement.

sources.title: FERPA or HIPAA for school student health records held by an outside provider
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.evidence_status: Official full page retrieved
sources.supports: Student health records maintained by a provider acting for a FERPA-covered school are education records under FERPA, rather than HIPAA records. A provider acting independently requires a different analysis, including HIPAA covered-entity status.
sources.limit: Record purpose and relationship determine the regime; school location alone does not. This does not establish a blanket BAA requirement.

sources.title: Background Checks: What Employers Need to Know
sources.publisher: Federal Trade Commission and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
sources.evidence_status: Official full page retrieved
sources.supports: Employment consumer reports require standalone disclosure and written authorization. Adverse-action processing includes pre-decision report/rights information and a subsequent notice. Equal-treatment, medical-inquiry and record-disposal requirements also apply as specified.
sources.limit: School fingerprinting, clearance, registries, employment-law coverage and state/local restrictions need separate research. The source does not establish a universal waiting interval.

sources.title: DOL Fact Sheet #22 — Hours Worked under the FLSA
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved; canonical direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: Compensable time can extend beyond scheduled work and include permitted work. Meal, training, waiting and travel treatment depend on the facts.
sources.limit: Employment status, exemption, overtime rules and state requirements remain unresolved; not every therapist or activity has the same pay treatment.

sources.title: DOL Fact Sheet #21 — FLSA recordkeeping
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved; direct fetch of indexed language URL returned 403
sources.supports: Covered employers maintain accurate employee, daily/weekly time and wage records. The federal baseline described includes three years for payroll records and two years for wage-computation supporting records.
sources.limit: These periods are not a universal retention schedule for student, credential, personnel or litigation records.

sources.title: IDEA §300.624 — Destruction of information
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved; direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: The public agency informs parents when IDEA Part B personal information is no longer needed for educational services; parental destruction requests then apply, with a specified permanent-record exception.
sources.limit: School counsel must reconcile the applicable duties, holds and record categories; vendor contract termination is not itself the complete retention rule.

requirements.title: Verify credentials against the discipline, state and school assignment
requirements.evidence_status: Official principle; proposed implementation; state-specific rules unresolved
requirements.applicability: SLP, OT or PT delivering IDEA Part B related services; requirements vary by state and professional role.
requirements.behavior: Maintain a versioned credential rule set keyed to state, discipline, school setting and role. Keep professional license, state education credential, national certification, clinical competence and district acceptance separate. Readiness remains unknown until authoritative verification and the applicable rule set are approved.
requirements.human_owner: Credentialing lead, state-licensed discipline supervisor and district special-education lead
open_questions: Which state board regulates SLP/OT/PT and which SEA school credentials or exemptions apply?
Which district qualifications, specialty experience and verification intervals apply?
requirements.acceptance: A synthetic valid national certification without the required state/school evidence cannot make a therapist ready. An expired, unmatched or unknown verification routes to review rather than being inferred valid.

requirements.title: Represent assistants and supervised practitioners as distinct roles
requirements.evidence_status: Official principle; proposed implementation; supervision rules unresolved
requirements.applicability: SLPA, OTA or PTA participation only where the selected state's rules and district arrangement permit it.
requirements.behavior: Store permitted tasks, required supervisor, supervision plan and evidence separately for each discipline. Prevent an assistant role from being used as an interchangeable substitute for an independently qualified therapist. Route provisional or unusual credentials for specialist interpretation; do not treat a credential label as an automatic legal conclusion.
requirements.human_owner: Discipline supervisor and district credentialing authority
open_questions: Which tasks, evaluation/signature permissions, supervision modes and ratios are permitted?
Are assistants included in the initial contract and do state/SEA rules impose additional restrictions?
requirements.acceptance: An assistant assignment without an approved supervisor or rule set cannot reach service-ready status; a generic supervisor field cannot satisfy a different discipline's supervision rules.

requirements.title: Use the authorized IEP service requirement as the operational input
requirements.evidence_status: Official IEP content; proposed data model
requirements.applicability: Services provided under an IDEA Part B IEP; other plans require their own applicability mapping.
requirements.behavior: Reference the school's authoritative plan version and effective dates. Capture the authorized service, frequency, duration, location, goal references and progress-report schedule without generating default clinical prescriptions. Store unclear or conflicting text as a question for the school team.
requirements.human_owner: District IEP team and qualified treating therapist
open_questions: Which IEP system is authoritative and which fields may be shared with the staffing platform?
How are amendments and effective dates communicated?
requirements.acceptance: A plan amendment preserves prior history and changes future operational requirements only after authorized verification. The system cannot insert standard minutes or goals because a field is missing.

requirements.title: Confirm provider access and responsibility handoff before service
requirements.evidence_status: Official principle; proposed workflow
requirements.applicability: A provider responsible for implementing an IEP, within the school's approved record-access basis.
requirements.behavior: Track whether the assigned provider can access the current IEP in the approved system and has received responsibility/accommodation information. Use an access reference when copying the IEP is unnecessary. Revalidate access when assignments end or change.
requirements.human_owner: School case manager, district records administrator and assigned therapist
open_questions: Who grants access and communicates changes?
Can the district provide a responsibility extract while preserving access to the complete IEP where required?
requirements.acceptance: A booked provider without confirmed access/responsibility handoff is flagged before service. Reassignment removes the prior worker's access and records the handoff.

requirements.title: Keep planned, attempted, delivered and missed service distinct
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed implementation derived from IEP service obligations
requirements.applicability: School therapy delivery tracking; the detailed documentation format is district- and discipline-dependent.
requirements.behavior: Keep separate service-obligation, scheduled-session, attendance/attempt and therapist-attested delivery records. Distinguish absence, closure, therapist unavailability and other interruption reasons. Escalate discrepancies to the school; do not automatically fabricate delivery or prescribe compensatory services.
requirements.human_owner: Treating therapist and district special-education lead
open_questions: How are group sessions and indirect work documented?
Who determines make-up or compensatory action, and what evidence/deadlines apply?
requirements.acceptance: A canceled session never becomes delivered merely because payroll time or an invoice exists. The system can identify an unresolved service gap while leaving the educational remedy to the authorized team.

requirements.title: Reserve clinical and educational decisions for authorized personnel
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed authority control grounded in qualified services and individualized plans
requirements.applicability: Evaluation, therapy judgments, IEP goals/services and progress conclusions.
requirements.behavior: Allow AI to organize evidence, draft documentation and surface scheduling gaps. Require the responsible qualified person or school process to attest clinical records and authorize changes. AI cannot autonomously determine eligibility, change goals/minutes/grouping or sign a therapist's note.
requirements.human_owner: Qualified therapist and district IEP team
open_questions: What drafting assistance does the district permit?
Which signatures, review steps and notices accompany each decision?
requirements.acceptance: An agent request to alter authorized service frequency or sign a clinical note is denied and audited. Draft text remains visibly unverified until the responsible person reviews it.

requirements.title: Establish student-record disclosure authority before connecting systems
requirements.evidence_status: Official disclosure conditions; proposed connection gate
requirements.applicability: PII from education records held by a FERPA-covered school.
requirements.behavior: Record the school's approved disclosure basis and approved recipients, including any AI/subprocessor. When using the school-official exception, document the institutional function, school control, purpose restrictions and legitimate educational interest. Keep the student-data connection disabled until this arrangement is established.
requirements.human_owner: District privacy/records officer and agency privacy counsel
open_questions: Does the school-official exception apply, or is another basis needed?
Which annual-notice criteria, state student-privacy terms, subprocessors and data locations apply?
requirements.acceptance: A signed commercial staffing agreement without an approved disclosure basis does not enable IEP import. An unapproved AI endpoint cannot receive student PII.

requirements.title: Enforce assignment-level access and purpose limits
requirements.evidence_status: Official access/use principle; proposed technical controls
requirements.applicability: School-approved access to student education records by staff, contractors and permitted systems.
requirements.behavior: Scope access by district, school, assignment and purpose. Keep student records out of worker recruiting and general payroll views. Audit accesses and exports as a product control; restrict reuse for model training, advertising or cross-client analysis unless separately authorized under applicable requirements.
requirements.human_owner: District records administrator and platform security owner
open_questions: Which roles need which student fields?
Which export, subprocessor and permitted-use controls are required by the district?
requirements.acceptance: Cross-district and unassigned-student access tests fail closed. A recruiter can see assignment readiness without seeing therapy notes. Revoked access also blocks agents and integration accounts.

requirements.title: Classify records by their actual school/provider relationship
requirements.evidence_status: Official FERPA/HIPAA distinction; proposed classification workflow
requirements.applicability: Student therapy records, agency employment records and any separate direct-to-patient business.
requirements.behavior: Classify datasets by record owner, purpose and whether the provider acts for the school. Apply the district-approved education-record controls to school records; evaluate independent healthcare activities separately. Keep worker medical/employment documents separate from student records. Do not declare all therapy data HIPAA or assume a BAA resolves FERPA.
requirements.human_owner: District privacy officer and agency privacy counsel
open_questions: Are any services delivered independently of the school?
Does the agency perform electronic covered transactions or other activities requiring a separate HIPAA analysis?
requirements.acceptance: A school-contracted session and an independent clinical encounter cannot inherit the same regime automatically. Unknown record classifications block downstream disclosure until reviewed.

requirements.title: Gate employment screening orders on the correct authorization
requirements.evidence_status: Official FCRA principle; proposed screening order control
requirements.applicability: Employment consumer reports obtained from a background reporting company; separate school clearance processes must also be assessed.
requirements.behavior: Require the approved standalone disclosure, written authorization and provider certification workflow before ordering a covered report. Store the document version, scope and event evidence. Treat consent for applicant screening, student-data disclosure and clinical services as different records.
requirements.human_owner: HR screening lead and employment counsel
open_questions: Which district/state fingerprinting, registry or clearance checks apply?
When may each check occur and what recheck authorization is needed?
requirements.acceptance: A general application checkbox or student-service consent cannot satisfy the configured screening authorization. Missing or out-of-scope authorization blocks the screening order.

requirements.title: Use a reviewed adverse-action and dispute process
requirements.evidence_status: Official notice principles; proposed human decision control
requirements.applicability: An employment decision based on covered consumer-report information; federal coverage and state/local rules require confirmation.
requirements.behavior: Route report issues to qualified HR review. Support pre-adverse report/rights delivery, an opportunity to contest, approved timing and a separately authorized final decision/notice. Apply reviewed job-related criteria consistently. Gate medical-inquiry workflows by an approved hiring-stage policy.
requirements.human_owner: HR decision maker and employment counsel
open_questions: Which notice forms, response periods and local restrictions apply?
Who handles disputed matches, accommodation requests and non-consumer-report school clearance decisions?
requirements.acceptance: A vendor flag cannot automatically reject an applicant. A timer alone cannot issue final adverse action. Tests preserve notices and candidate responses without revealing sensitive details to unrelated users.

requirements.title: Separate paid work, contract billing and student service measures
requirements.evidence_status: Official time/record principles; proposed ledger separation
requirements.applicability: Agency employees subject to applicable wage rules; the employer, classification and pay model remain unresolved.
requirements.behavior: Maintain raw work-time evidence and separate payroll, customer-billable and student-service records. Capture preparation, documentation, meetings, training, travel and interrupted breaks for classification under approved rules. Do not erase worked time because a district rejects an invoice or a student session was canceled.
requirements.human_owner: Payroll lead, employment counsel and district contract owner
open_questions: Who employs each therapist; which exemption, workweek aggregation, rates and state wage rules apply?
Which activities are billable under the contract?
requirements.acceptance: A synthetic therapist with work at two client sites retains both time records. Invoice rejection does not silently zero payroll time; paid preparation does not count as delivered therapy minutes.

requirements.title: Support district-led record access, correction and retention
requirements.evidence_status: Official record principles; proposed lifecycle controls
requirements.applicability: Separate student/IDEA, personnel, consumer-report and payroll record categories.
requirements.behavior: Maintain category-specific retention policies, requests, holds and approved destruction/export workflows. Route student access/correction requests to the school and preserve amendment history. Reconcile IDEA no-longer-needed/destruction duties with applicable holds. Do not apply payroll retention periods to all data or delete student records automatically at contract end.
requirements.human_owner: District records officer, agency HR/payroll records owners and counsel
open_questions: Which state schedules, legal holds, parent/eligible-student requests and contract return/destruction terms apply?
Who owns the authoritative record and each authorized copy?
requirements.acceptance: An outstanding records-access request blocks affected deletion. A payroll retention rule cannot destroy an IEP record. An approved deletion action records categories, authority and affected replicas.

requirements.title: Keep incomplete qualifications or unresolved service conditions visible
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed readiness control derived from personnel and service obligations
requirements.applicability: Launch and each therapist-to-school assignment.
requirements.behavior: Maintain readiness dimensions for professional qualification, district clearance, supervision, authorized service input and system access. Unknown is distinct from failed and approved. Agents can request evidence and escalate; they cannot bypass missing state or school rules to mark a worker fully ready.
requirements.human_owner: Agency credentialing lead and district accountable service owner
open_questions: Who accepts residual exceptions, where legally permitted?
What prevents a placement from starting before unresolved launch conditions are resolved?
requirements.acceptance: Every production assignment has a rule version and named accountable approval. An unresolved state credential or supervision rule cannot be converted into readiness by a commercial deadline.

production_blocking_unknowns.needed: Select the state and client, confirm public/charter/private status and whether the work is IDEA Part B, another school framework or direct clinical care.

production_blocking_unknowns.owner: District HR/safeguarding lead and employment counsel

production_blocking_unknowns.owner: District special-education lead and qualified therapists

production_blocking_unknowns.needed: Determine employer, work authorization/onboarding, worker classification, wage/overtime rules, aggregation across assignments, pay timing, leave and recordkeeping duties before production payroll.
Approve disclosure basis, district IEP system ownership, AI/subprocessor access, tenant boundaries, state student-privacy conditions and records lifecycle.
production_blocking_unknowns.owner: District privacy officer and platform security lead

discipline_discovery_checklist.research: Identify the state speech-language pathology/audiology authority, SEA credential or school-specific exemption pathway, permitted SLPA work and supervision. Verify any national certification/client requirement separately; it is not a substitute for state authority.
discipline_discovery_checklist.evidence_to_obtain: Board/SEA rule links, verification method, district qualification schedule, supervisor evidence and sample role-specific service documentation.

discipline_discovery_checklist.research: Identify the state occupational therapy authority and school requirements, practice scope, OTA delegation/supervision, evaluation and signature permissions. Do not reuse SLP rules.
discipline_discovery_checklist.evidence_to_obtain: Board/SEA requirements, district role description, approved supervision arrangement and documentation standards.

discipline_discovery_checklist.research: Identify the state physical therapy authority and school requirements, PTA supervision, evaluation and signature permissions, and any relevant service/referral constraints. Do not reuse OT rules.
discipline_discovery_checklist.evidence_to_obtain: Board/SEA requirements, district role description, approved supervision arrangement and documentation standards.

discipline_discovery_checklist.research: Identify plan authority, provider responsibility handoff, student-service consent confirmation, progress reporting, transfers and missed-service escalation.
discipline_discovery_checklist.evidence_to_obtain: De-identified IEP/service-order example, access workflow, version-change notification and exception SOP.

discipline_discovery_checklist.research: Confirm school/record coverage, disclosure authority, approved AI recipients, access matrix and request/retention/destruction duties.
discipline_discovery_checklist.evidence_to_obtain: Approved data agreement, district annual-notice criteria, state privacy terms and record schedule.

discipline_discovery_checklist.research: Confirm screening and school clearance, worker onboarding/classification, time categories, overtime aggregation and pay/billing separation.
discipline_discovery_checklist.evidence_to_obtain: Approved disclosure/authorization and notice templates, client clearance schedule, time policy and sample corrected payroll/invoice case.

requirements.title: Use an edition-specific integration contract
requirements.actor: Integration owner
requirements.trigger: Selecting or changing an ATS/payroll adapter
requirements.required_behavior: Record the product/version, authorized fields, operations, scopes, supported test method and export path before enabling writes.
requirements.exception: Missing entitlement or ambiguous write semantics keeps the adapter simulated or read-only within allowed scope.
requirements.acceptance: A required unavailable operation produces a failed conformance result, not a claimed working connector.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed behavior based on vendor documentation

requirements.title: Verify applicable AI integration permission
requirements.actor: Procurement and integration owner
requirements.trigger: Connecting an agent to a vendor service
requirements.required_behavior: Record the governing agreement and approved AI/data purpose for the actual selected product.
requirements.exception: Unresolved terms prevent enabling that use; do not infer access from another customer's account or generic API availability.
requirements.acceptance: Configuration requires a dated permission/terms decision for the actual vendor/product.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed gate informed by published vendor policy

requirements.title: Match screening order to permitted package and consent
requirements.actor: Credential reviewer
requirements.required_behavior: Use provider identity, applicable school package, consent evidence and an approved transaction; store a restricted report reference.
requirements.exception: Wrong package, missing authority or mismatch routes to review and must not auto-order or auto-reject.
requirements.acceptance: Duplicate order retries cannot create a second charge and incomplete authority prevents submission.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed design; legal requirements separately mapped in obligations

requirements.title: Keep actual work, service evidence and billing separate
requirements.actor: Payroll and billing owners
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain independent worked-time and contract-billable calculations, with original records, unit types and versioned corrections.
requirements.exception: Invoice rejection cannot by itself suppress worked-time evaluation or earned-pay processing.
requirements.acceptance: A disputed service/invoice line leaves the corresponding pay preparation independently reviewable.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed operating requirement; source-specific contract and obligations pack constrain implementation

requirements.title: Make external actions idempotent and reconcilable
requirements.actor: Agent gateway and integration owner
requirements.trigger: Write, retry or uncertain vendor response
requirements.required_behavior: Persist operation key, payload/version hash and external acknowledgment. Reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying a non-idempotent operation.
requirements.exception: Timeout is not evidence of failure; retain unknown state with an owner.
requirements.acceptance: Repeated identical actions produce one business effect; changed payload under the same key is rejected.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed architecture requirement

requirements.title: Bind approval to the exact action
requirements.actor: Named district, clinical, employment or financial approver
requirements.required_behavior: Store actor, scope, payload hash, record versions, policy version, expiry and revocation state; block stale approvals.
requirements.exception: Any material change requires new approval by the appropriate owner.
requirements.acceptance: A changed rate, recipient, evidence version or amount invalidates the earlier approval.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed authority control

requirements.title: Minimize school data and isolate tenants
requirements.actor: District privacy owner and platform owner
requirements.trigger: Any import, search, export or message
requirements.required_behavior: Enforce approved field purposes and role/district boundaries server-side. Keep clinical and IEP content in the school-designated record system for this initial scope.
requirements.exception: Even opaque student references require approved access and handling; unapproved content is quarantined or excluded.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-district requests and general recruiter access to student service content fail without leaking data in results or logs.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed design; FERPA applicability addressed in obligations

requirements.title: Version district rules and resolve conflicts
requirements.actor: District contract owner
requirements.trigger: New order, amendment or conflicting instruction
requirements.required_behavior: Record source, effective interval, scope, approved interpretation and precedence for each rule; recalculate only affected records.
requirements.exception: Conflicting percentages, units or deadlines remain unresolved until the owner confirms the governing rule.
requirements.acceptance: Two incompatible clauses create a visible blocked configuration item; the agent cannot choose the more convenient one.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed design; public district examples are requirements evidence only

requirements.title: Plan workload beyond direct service minutes
requirements.actor: Qualified therapy lead and scheduler
requirements.required_behavior: Include approved direct service, assessment, documentation, meetings, supervision, travel and other duties in the workload profile.
requirements.exception: Do not infer universal capacity from a student count or assume all paid work is a therapy session.
requirements.acceptance: An apparently free session slot is rejected or reviewed when approved indirect duties or travel consume that capacity.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed system behavior informed by professional guidance

requirements.title: Apply discipline and school qualifications independently
requirements.actor: Credential owner
requirements.required_behavior: Evaluate the selected discipline, provider/assistant level, state/SEA requirements, supervision and district acceptance with dated evidence.
requirements.exception: A professional certificate alone is not assumed to meet every state or district requirement; nursing verification cannot clear therapists.
requirements.acceptance: A provider qualified for one role or district is not automatically marked ready for another.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed design informed by provider qualification guidance

requirements.title: Keep district invoicing distinct from Medicaid claims
requirements.actor: Commercial and billing owners
requirements.required_behavior: Produce district staffing invoices under executed terms. Treat any Medicaid claiming product as a separate future decision with state/program/provider/documentation requirements.
requirements.exception: An invoice, service record or professional license is not treated as proof of Medicaid claim eligibility.
requirements.acceptance: The initial product has no enabled Medicaid claim submission route and labels its financial outputs as district invoices.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed scope decision informed by CMS guidance structure

requirements.title: Treat imported documents as evidence, not commands
requirements.actor: Agent gateway
requirements.trigger: Uploaded resume, contract, message or school-system content
requirements.required_behavior: Keep extracted facts separate from action instructions. Only validated application commands and approved policy can authorize an action.
requirements.exception: Embedded instructions to alter recipients, rates, credentials or permissions are ignored and flagged.
requirements.acceptance: A hostile instruction in a synthetic document cannot change an approved rate, export data or grant access.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed AI security requirement

requirements.title: Set measurable operational and recovery targets
requirements.actor: Operations and technical owners
requirements.required_behavior: Agree response coverage, access revocation timing, recovery time, recovery point, expected peak volume and reconciled error-handling targets; measure them against the implementation.
requirements.exception: Unset targets and untested recovery remain open readiness items.
requirements.acceptance: A vendor-outage and restoration drill preserves pending work and reconciles delayed events without duplicate financial effects.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed nonfunctional requirement; thresholds not yet selected

requirements.title: Define retention, offboarding and export by data class
requirements.actor: District privacy owner and operator records owner
requirements.trigger: Provisioning, contract end or deletion request
requirements.required_behavior: Assign an approved retention schedule and hold rules separately to staffing, education, screening, financial and audit records; revoke access and reconcile exports at offboarding.
requirements.exception: Do not use one invented retention period or remove held records automatically.
requirements.acceptance: Synthetic offboarding revokes the right access, exports only authorized records and preserves items under an applicable hold.
requirements.evidence_status: Proposed design; jurisdiction and contract review pending

transitions.on_exception: AI cannot approve; changed hash requires new review.

transitions.evidence_required: Approval hash, provider mapping and idempotency key.

REJECTED/VOIDED do not cancel worker-pay obligations.

transitions.output: New draft version.

transitions.evidence_required: Exact payload approval.
transitions.output: Current issue authorization.
transitions.on_exception: No model-only issue approval in initial pilot.

transitions.prerequisites: Matching approval; durable unique outbox and external invoice operation; ISSUED only on confirmed provider issue.

transitions.output: Issued immutable provider mirror and delivery evidence.
transitions.on_exception: Timeout stays AUTHORIZED with command outcome unknown and dispatch lock; lookup before retry; block edit/void while pending.

Issue/release failures cannot silently change payroll state.

invariants: School/student safety concerns immediately route through the approved staffed school/clinical/emergency pathway; agents do not diagnose, determine eligibility or change therapy.
School owns student clinical/service plans and records; staffing case stores only minimal authorized reference/status.

permission_matrix.conditions: Verified identity; only own records and worker-safe projection.
Active worksite/action delegation; masked worker projection.
Credential scope plus necessary clinical/HR decision references; no implied professional authority.

Readiness outcome only; no waiver of missing credential/terms.

Case membership; substantive decisions within separately granted authority.

responses.unknown_external: 202 pending reconciliation with stable operation key; never claim successful effect.

tenant_and_storage_controls: Tenant row scopes and foreign-key checks apply to database, queues, object storage, search/vector index, caches, exports and logs.

Cross-tenant or cross-client record discovery returns no existence/detail leak; authorization evaluated before search and retrieval.
No production personal records in test fixtures or model evaluation by default; use synthetic workers.
Student clinical/service records are out of scope. Incident intake minimizes identifiers and routes necessary care details to authorized clinical channels.
Break-glass sensitive access requires explicit time-limited purpose, independent owner authorization and alert/audit; never agent self-grant.
Offboarding revokes tokens/delegations and scheduled actions; outstanding payroll/case obligations remain assigned.

School/district boundary applies to all provider projections and service references. Student-level service data stays in the school-authorized system; opaque references/approved aggregates must not permit unauthorized lookup or re-identification.

retention_policy_pointers.required_configuration: Purpose, applicable employment/consent rules, consent text, trigger, retention period, access scope and rights handling.
Applicable agreement/legal record requirements, effective version history, audit purpose, expiry trigger and hold rules.
Category-specific access, location and applicable record rules; store status/reference instead of report where sufficient.
Applicable jurisdiction/employer/time/wage/tax/accounting schedules and dispute holds; no erasure of owed-pay evidence.
Case class, necessary evidence, access, investigation/claim holds and disposal approval.
Minimum traceability and provider reconciliation window, masking, retention, immutable archive and controlled deletion.

domain_specification.retention_boundary: Launch requires approved category schedules, hold precedence and deletion/backup evidence. No legal periods invented. Withdrawal alone does not erase valid-purpose records.

checks: Every state reachable and every nonterminal has a terminal path
Public listing never creates client authority
validation_contract.execution_status: Structural design checks only; adapters, jurisdiction rules and operating behavior untested.

domain_specification.command_input_type_rule: Inputs resolve to object fields; *_ref=reference, *_refs=array<reference>, *_id=uuid, *_hash=sha256, *_key=string, *_interval=zoned_interval, closure_reason=string. Validate adapter payload schemas before implementation.

scenario_pack.title: School-based therapy staffing: synthetic acceptance scenarios
scenario_pack.status: Proposed requirements fixtures; product acceptance tests not implemented or executed
scenario_pack.scope: A proposed school-based therapy staffing pilot using SLP as the worked example, with explicit OT/PT and assistant-role variation. State and employer model remain unselected. These fixtures are proposed requirements, not recovered Amergis procedures.
scenario_pack.data_classification: Entirely synthetic; no real provider, license, school, student, IEP, diagnosis, service record, payroll or bank data
scenario_pack.authority_note: Named roles are proposed accountable functions, not identified employees. Owners must be appointed and approve applicable policies before a live pilot.
scenario_pack.state_model_note: State labels refer to the proposed DS-SM01 through DS-SM09 domain models. An expected state is an assertion for a future acceptance test, not a transition performed by this artifact.
assumptions: Use one hypothetical school/district tenant and an SLP staffing work block as the worked example. OT, PT and assistant roles require separate applicable qualification and supervision rules, not copied SLP assumptions.
All orders, providers, evidence and financial values are artificial. No external vendor is called.
The launch state, employer model, school requirements and applicable pay rules remain selection and qualified-review items. These fixtures do not assert legal compliance.

Readiness is established only from the selected approved discipline/role/school requirement pack and a designated qualified reviewer. Uploading a document is not verification; an assistant cannot inherit a licensed therapist scope.

The staffing MVP retains only minimum authorized school-owned service-record references and approved aggregates. It does not replicate a student IEP/EHR or generate diagnoses, treatment plans or service-entitlement decisions.

School service calendars, provider worked time, direct-service minutes, documentation/travel activities and invoice quantities remain separate. Service-minute totals cannot automatically determine pay hours or billing units.

Financial examples deliberately use artificial hourly staffing rates and simple arithmetic. No inference is made about minimum wage, overtime, breaks, cancellation pay, premiums, tax, deductions, burden, reimbursement eligibility or profit.
Payroll eligibility, payroll authorization, school time approval and invoice status are separate facts. A service-record gap or invoice dispute must not automatically withhold provider pay.
Scheduled intervals include an IANA time zone and UTC instants. The duration fixture supplies explicit offsets for a clock-change example; elapsed time is not automatically payable time.

An AI agent may prepare information and perform specifically delegated administrative actions. It cannot change an IEP, make a clinical or educational service decision, assume supervision authority or authorize financial release.

Readable fixture labels such as SYN-PROVIDER-A are symbolic aliases. Implementation must map them to valid canonical identifiers, including UUIDs where required by the domain schema, and validate complete request payloads. These scenarios are not ready-to-send API payloads.

scenarios.title: Provider has not granted the required school-submission consent
prerequisites: The proposed policy requires active purpose-specific consent before provider information is submitted to the named school.
Provider SYN-C01 exists; no client submission has been made.
expected_state_or_action: Keep the submission in DRAFT and prevent delivery.
Present the consent request with recipient and purpose; record the provider's actual choice before any later submission.
forbidden_outcomes: Treating a publicly visible profile or prior unrelated consent as this authorization
Sending the profile before consent
Manufacturing an affirmative consent event
scenarios.accountable_owner: Provider privacy and recruiting owner
acceptance_checks: No outbound client payload exists.
The audit records the missing purpose-specific consent and denied action.
Consent text version and recipient are available for a subsequent affirmative choice.
scenarios.future_test_type: End-to-end consent and outbound-delivery test with synthetic identities

scenarios.title: Possible duplicate provider requires identity reconciliation
prerequisites: SYN-C02A and SYN-C02B are separate records within the same operator scope.
One shared contact detail is a possible duplicate signal, not a verified identity match.

inputs.conflict: different supplied credential identity and role classification

expected_state_or_action: Create a restricted duplicate-review case and preserve both record IDs.
Permit an authorized reviewer to resolve the identity conflict; if a merge is later approved, retain lineage and field provenance.
forbidden_outcomes: Automatic destructive merge
Cross-tenant record disclosure
Silently transferring consent or credential clearance between people
scenarios.accountable_owner: Identity and data stewardship owner
acceptance_checks: Both source records and conflicting values remain retrievable by the authorized reviewer.
No readiness or consent status is inherited from the potential duplicate.
Any later merge requires a recorded reviewer decision and reversible lineage.
scenarios.future_test_type: Identity matching, merge authorization and audit integration test

scenarios.title: Consent withdrawal reaches queued actions
prerequisites: A provider has ACTIVE consent for a specific client submission purpose.
A related outbound submission is queued but not delivered.
expected_state_or_action: Record WITHDRAWN consent and cancel the affected queued delivery.
Evaluate already completed sharing and record retention separately under the approved policy; expose a case to the privacy owner when required.
forbidden_outcomes: Executing a stale queued submission
Claiming withdrawal retracts information already delivered
Deleting all audit and financial records without a retention decision
scenarios.accountable_owner: Provider privacy owner
acceptance_checks: Execution-time authorization reads the current consent version.
The canceled action records the withdrawal event ID.
Future purposes and any retention decision are evaluated explicitly, not inferred.
scenarios.future_test_type: Event ordering and consent revocation race test

scenarios.title: Incomplete discipline and school credential evidence cannot produce readiness
prerequisites: The synthetic school's selected SLP requirement pack requires role-appropriate authoritative credential verification and a school-approved onboarding record. The actual state-specific requirements are unresolved.
Only an uploaded credential image is present.
expected_state_or_action: Keep readiness INCOMPLETE and list the missing evidence with source and owner.
Request missing evidence through the approved channel; do not mark the proposed school work block ready.
forbidden_outcomes: Equating OCR completion with verification
Marking READY from a marketing profile
Inventing missing dates or credential values
scenarios.accountable_owner: Credentialing owner and designated qualified discipline/school reviewer
acceptance_checks: Each unmet requirement is individually visible.
Evidence origin and verification status differ in the record.
A confirm/start action is denied with a reviewable reason.
scenarios.future_test_type: Requirement-pack evaluation and readiness guard test

scenarios.title: Credential identity mismatch is unresolved evidence
prerequisites: The provider identity and authoritative response use conflicting synthetic identifiers.
No qualified reviewer has resolved the mismatch.
expected_state_or_action: Keep readiness INCOMPLETE, route the identity mismatch to the authorized reviewer, and restrict the evidence to that review scope.
Ask for identity reconciliation through the approved process; retain the original response.
forbidden_outcomes: Overwriting the provider with a different person's result
Automatic employment rejection
Disclosing full sensitive evidence to an unrelated client user
scenarios.accountable_owner: Credentialing and employment review owner
acceptance_checks: The mismatch remains explicit in the decision evidence.
No READY state is asserted.
The reviewer can identify both original values and their sources.
scenarios.future_test_type: Identity mismatch, reviewer routing and evidence access test

scenarios.title: Required evidence expires during the proposed school work block
prerequisites: For this synthetic case, the approved requirement pack explicitly requires the credential to remain valid through the work-block end. This is a chosen fixture, not a universal jurisdiction rule.
A confirmed assignment has not started.
A previously approved readiness snapshot no longer covers the full revised work-block interval; the domain expiry guard is being evaluated for that interval.
expected_state_or_action: Mark readiness EXPIRED for this work-block interval and place the confirmed assignment on HOLD.
Notify the credential and school staffing owners; require verified renewal or an explicitly permitted qualified resolution before start.
forbidden_outcomes: Checking validity only at onboarding
Extending the credential date
Allowing an agent to approve its own exception
scenarios.accountable_owner: Credentialing owner and school discipline/supervision contact
acceptance_checks: The rule version and evaluated shift interval are retained.
Expiry is compared as an instant, with original time-zone context preserved.
The start guard remains closed until an authorized resolution is recorded.
scenarios.future_test_type: Time-dependent readiness invalidation and assignment guard test

scenarios.title: Assistant scope and supervision cannot substitute for a licensed role
prerequisites: The synthetic school requisition requires a licensed SLP role. A submitted provider profile is an assistant role.
No approved role substitution, supervision configuration or delegated scope exists. OT/PT assistant variants must use their own separately reviewed rules.
Assistant/trainee placement is outside this initial pilot until a separate approved discipline/jurisdiction/school scope matrix exists; no qualified readiness decision is yet recorded.
expected_state_or_action: Keep readiness INCOMPLETE, prevent automatic confirmation and route the scope/supervision gap to the qualified school/discipline reviewer. A BLOCKED determination requires the separate complete-evidence and explicit qualified-reviewer path.
Evaluate qualification, supervision and allowed tasks using a separately approved role/jurisdiction/school rule set. A named supervisor alone is not proof of a valid arrangement.
forbidden_outcomes: Treating assistant and licensed therapist credentials as interchangeable
Allowing an agent to invent or accept a supervision arrangement
Copying SLP scope rules to OT or PT without discipline-specific review
Automatically changing the school order to fit the available provider
scenarios.accountable_owner: Qualified discipline/supervision reviewer and school staffing owner
acceptance_checks: The requested discipline and role remain unchanged.
Each assistant variation is denied until its approved requirements are satisfied.
No confirmation occurs merely because the assistant has a credential or a supervisor name.
scenarios.future_test_type: Discipline-role matching, supervision evidence and assignment guard test

scenarios.title: School submission approval is bound to the exact provider, role and version
prerequisites: Provider consent is ACTIVE for the named school and role.
A reviewer approved submission version 3 with a specific payload digest.
expected_state_or_action: Keep the revised submission DRAFT until version 4 receives the required approval.
Show the changed field and invalidate the stale approval for execution.
forbidden_outcomes: Sending a different payload under version 3 approval
Treating chat approval as a standing unlimited grant
Changing the recipient after approval
scenarios.accountable_owner: Recruiting submission owner
acceptance_checks: Approval binds provider, client, role, payload digest and version.
A version mismatch produces no outbound delivery.
The new proposal and approval lineage remain visible.
scenarios.future_test_type: Version-bound approval and outbound submission test

scenarios.title: Itinerant provider work blocks conflict across time zones
prerequisites: A synthetic SLP already has a confirmed school work block.
The provider requests an overlapping second work block. Travel time, supervision availability and school calendars are additional separately selected constraints.

duration_example.purpose: Artificial timestamp parser edge case only; not a proposed school service schedule or pay entitlement.

expected_state_or_action: Detect 30 minutes of overlap after conversion to UTC and deny confirmation of the second shift.
Offer the conflict for review without canceling the existing assignment.
For the separate explicit-offset clock-change edge case, calculate four elapsed hours. Reject repeated local clock labels lacking offset/fold as insufficient input.
Evaluate school calendar, travel and supervision constraints separately; non-overlap alone does not prove feasible service coverage.
forbidden_outcomes: Comparing only local clock labels
Double-booking
Silently canceling either assignment to make the conflict disappear
Treating elapsed duration or non-overlap as proof of pay eligibility, travel feasibility or school service compliance
scenarios.accountable_owner: Scheduling owner
acceptance_checks: Overlap is 30 minutes for the supplied instants.
The original zones and UTC instants are preserved.
Any additional travel/rest eligibility is evaluated separately from interval overlap.
The separate clock-change fixture yields 240 elapsed minutes; this is not a paid-duration conclusion.
Preserve source timestamp offsets and require clarification of ambiguous local events.
scenarios.future_test_type: Scheduling interval and confirmation guard test

scenarios.title: School calendar closure changes planned work without inventing services
scenarios.actor: School calendar user and scheduling agent
prerequisites: A school work block is CONFIRMED under calendar revision 6 and has not started.
The school supplies an authorized closure in revision 7. No cancellation fee or provider pay determination has been approved.
expected_state_or_action: Apply HOLD or an authorized CANCELLED transition according to the selected school contract and notify the provider. Preserve calendar versions and the original assignment.
Create no delivered-service record for a closed/canceled session. Reopening creates a reviewable scheduling proposal rather than silently restoring the old assignment.
Route compensation and any customer cancellation charge separately. A charge requires an explicit applicable approved contract rule; the fixture assumes no such charge.
forbidden_outcomes: Fabricating delivered therapy or attendance
Automatically restoring a canceled work block after a calendar edit
Automatically charging a closure fee or zeroing provider pay
Erasing any actual work recorded before a late closure notice
scenarios.accountable_owner: School calendar/staffing owner, with separate payroll and billing owners
acceptance_checks: The affected work block links to the closure and calendar revision.
No service-delivery event or automatic fee appears.
A reopening request rechecks provider availability, readiness, school approval and capacity.
scenarios.future_test_type: School calendar version, closure and assignment lifecycle integration test

scenarios.title: Concurrent confirmations cannot overfill a school staffing position
prerequisites: One authorized school staffing position remains open; it is staffing capacity, not a student service entitlement.
Two individually eligible providers concurrently request confirmation.
expected_state_or_action: Use a single atomic capacity/reservation decision so only one confirmation succeeds.
Return a clear capacity conflict to the losing request and preserve both attempt records.
forbidden_outcomes: Two confirmed assignments against capacity one
Charging or notifying a losing provider as confirmed
Deleting the losing request audit
scenarios.accountable_owner: Scheduling owner and platform transaction owner
acceptance_checks: Confirmed count is at most one after concurrent execution and retries.
The winning reservation has one stable logical ID.
Both providers receive status consistent with the authoritative record.
scenarios.future_test_type: Concurrency, reservation and event-delivery integration test

scenarios.title: Missed therapy session creates a makeup proposal without changing the IEP
scenarios.actor: School service coordinator and scheduling agent
prerequisites: The school-owned service system reports a missed session using an authorized reference and minimal scheduling aggregate.
The school/qualified clinician owns service requirements and makeup decisions; the staffing platform does not hold or edit the IEP.
expected_state_or_action: Keep the original session recorded as missed in the source-owned record; retain only the approved reference and coordination status in the staffing platform.
Prepare a makeup scheduling proposal for school/qualified clinician approval and evaluate provider readiness, calendar, capacity and supervision.
Do not infer required makeup minutes, alter service entitlement, or represent the proposal as delivered care.
forbidden_outcomes: Automatic IEP edits or clinical service decisions
Automatically confirming a makeup session solely to close an exception
Changing the missed session to delivered
Pulling an entire IEP or diagnosis into agent context when a reference is sufficient
scenarios.accountable_owner: School service coordinator and qualified treating/supervising clinician
acceptance_checks: The proposal has an approval state and no delivered-service claim.
The school-owned record remains authoritative for service status and requirements.
The original missed event and final coordination decision remain linked without unnecessary student information.
scenarios.future_test_type: Missed-session coordination, makeup approval and minimum-data integration test

scenarios.title: Provider absence creates a coverage case and preserves undelivered sessions
prerequisites: An approved provider work block is due to start.
A missing check-in is a signal, not a confirmed absence; the school-owned schedule remains authoritative for affected service records.

inputs.provider_reply: arrival delayed; school contact not reached

expected_state_or_action: Open an incident, contact the provider and the designated school/on-duty staffing owner, and reconcile the facts.
Prepare a qualified replacement or rescheduling proposal under school approval. Do not auto-assign an available person without role, supervision, readiness and capacity checks.
Keep unfilled services undelivered; record NO_SHOW only after an authorized factual determination and preserve any actual worked time.
forbidden_outcomes: Automatically assigning NO_SHOW from a missing app event
Recording service as delivered because a replacement search started
Automatic discipline or payroll withholding
Unapproved role substitution
Unnecessary student-detail disclosure in coverage messages
scenarios.accountable_owner: On-duty staffing coordinator and school service contact
acceptance_checks: Contact attempts and conflicting accounts remain visible.
An explicit on-duty escalation owner receives the case.
Replacement approval, affected-service references, provider time and any employment decision have separate histories.
scenarios.future_test_type: Provider absence, authorized coverage and service-status reconciliation test

scenarios.title: Approved worked hours produce staffing financial preparation, separate from service minutes
prerequisites: The payroll owner has classified the supplied synthetic pay hours for preparation.
The billing owner has accepted the supplied synthetic bill hours and artificial rate version.
Calculation is preparation only; no funds or invoice are released.

inputs.billing_basis: explicit artificial staffed-hour contract, not student service units

expected_state_or_action: Prepare pay of USD 340.00 and a bill draft of USD 490.00 using FIN01.
Attach hours, rate version and rounding policy to each amount; await the relevant release authority.

Retain 360 direct-service minutes and 120 other approved work minutes as separate artificial aggregates; do not derive individual student entitlement, treatment units or reimbursement from the staffing amount.
forbidden_outcomes: Floating-point monetary drift
Calling the USD 150.00 rate difference profit
Releasing payment or issuing an invoice from calculation alone
Multiplying a group session by student count to inflate provider hours or assuming direct-service minutes equal paid or billed hours
scenarios.accountable_owner: Payroll and billing owners
acceptance_checks: Decimal results equal stored fixture amounts.

scenarios.title: Corrected time and attendance preserve separate histories and financial adjustments
scenarios.actor: Provider, time reviewer and finance preparation agent
prerequisites: Revision 1 used FIN02 prior amounts and has already been settled/issued in the hypothetical records.
A designated reviewer accepts revision 2 with 8.25 hours for this artificial example.

inputs.reason: synthetic end-time correction plus separate school-owned service-attendance correction

expected_state_or_action: Retain revision 1 and its original settlement references.
Prepare revised totals of USD 350.63 pay and USD 505.31 bill; prepare separately authorized adjustments of USD 10.63 and USD 15.31.
Require approvals for the adjustment payload; do not replay the original total payment or rewrite an issued invoice.
Link the school-owned service correction separately from the provider time revision; fewer direct-service minutes do not automatically reduce independently classified worked hours.
forbidden_outcomes: Mutating settled history
Paying the entire revised total as an additional payment
Reusing old approval for a new amount
Dropping the provider correction because a prior invoice was issued
Rewriting student attendance or service delivery from provider time alone
scenarios.accountable_owner: School service-record owner, time review, payroll and billing owners
acceptance_checks: The version chain includes author, reason, accepted time facts and decision.
Delta equals rounded revised total minus rounded prior total for each ledger.
Each adjustment has a new logical ID linked to its original and exact approval.
scenarios.future_test_type: Versioned time correction, financial adjustment and audit integration test

scenarios.title: A school invoice dispute does not automatically stop provider payroll
scenarios.actor: Client billing user and finance exception agent
prerequisites: The payroll owner has authorized the synthetic provider pay amount using valid worked-time evidence.
The customer disputes the separately issued invoice.
expected_state_or_action: Move the invoice to DISPUTED with USD 495.00 remaining as the disputed amount pending resolution.
Keep USD 330.00 provider payroll preparation/authorization unchanged by this billing event.
Route billing investigation to its owner; investigate any independent pay issue on its own evidence.
forbidden_outcomes: Automatic withholding or voiding provider pay because the customer disputed an invoice
Changing the disputed invoice amount to zero without an approved adjustment
Claiming a dispute has been resolved merely because payroll progressed
scenarios.accountable_owner: Billing owner, with a separate payroll owner
acceptance_checks: An invoice dispute event causes no payroll amount/state mutation.
The dispute reason, owner and disputed balance are visible.
Any subsequent credit or adjustment requires its own approved payload.
scenarios.future_test_type: Cross-ledger isolation and billing-dispute workflow test

scenarios.title: Worked time, direct-service minutes and accepted billing hours remain separate
scenarios.actor: Time review and financial preparation agents
prerequisites: For this artificial fixture, the payroll owner classified 7.75 hours for pay preparation.
The customer accepted 7.50 hours for billing; another 0.25 bill hours remain under review.

inputs.billing_basis: explicit artificial staffed-hour contract; no student service-unit or reimbursement inference

group_session_unit_example.purpose: Four synthetic attendance references for one group session do not create 120 provider service minutes. Student service accounting remains school-owned; no billing-unit inference.

expected_state_or_action: Prepare USD 328.60 pay and USD 477.00 accepted-hours bill draft.
Retain USD 15.90 as a pending billing calculation for the extra 0.25 hours, with its own disposition.
Continue the payroll workflow independently of the unresolved billing portion.
Preserve the separately reported 360 direct-service, 60 documentation and 45 travel minutes; these sum to the owner-classified 465 worked minutes in this chosen fixture only.
forbidden_outcomes: Reducing provider pay hours to customer-approved bill hours
Automatically invoicing the pending portion
Discarding the extra worked-time evidence
Using direct-service minutes as a substitute for worked time
Multiplying group-session duration by student count to determine provider compensation
Automatically converting service minutes to reimbursable units
scenarios.accountable_owner: Payroll owner and billing owner
acceptance_checks: Separate pay_hours, accepted_bill_hours and pending_bill_hours remain queryable.
The pending bill amount is not included in the ready-to-issue bill draft.
No client-approval dependency blocks the independently authorized pay-preparation path.
The fixture minutes sum to 465, while accepted billing hours remain 7.50 and pending billing hours remain 0.25.
A 30-minute group session with four synthetic attendance references remains 30 provider service minutes; any student-level accounting remains in the school-owned source.
scenarios.future_test_type: Separate time classifications and financial preparation integration test

scenarios.title: Timed-out financial submission is reconciled before retry
prerequisites: An exact payroll payload was authorized and submitted once with a stable idempotency key.
The client timed out; provider acceptance is unknown.
expected_state_or_action: Move the operation into RECONCILING and query the approved status/reconciliation path.
Link the provider's accepted transaction to the original operation; do not submit a second logical payment.
If a supported retry is necessary, retain the same key and exact approved payload under the connector contract.

Treating a timeout as proof of failure
Treating provider acceptance as proof of settlement
Altering the amount while preserving the old approval

acceptance_checks: At most one provider financial transaction exists for the logical operation.
Attempt history and provider reference are retained.
The state advances only on evidence appropriate to accepted, settled or rejected status.
scenarios.future_test_type: Fault injection, idempotency and provider reconciliation contract test

scenarios.title: Credential vendor outage cannot create a false verification
prerequisites: A fresh authoritative role/jurisdiction credential check is required by the selected discipline and school rule pack.

expected_state_or_action: Record the failed attempt and keep readiness INCOMPLETE because required fresh verification is unresolved; route any time-sensitive assignment to its owner.
Queue a bounded retry under connector policy, then reconcile the returned response to the original provider and request.
Require the normal readiness decision after successful evidence retrieval.

Silently treating stale evidence as fresh
Creating duplicate screening/check orders
Dropping unresolved requests on recovery
scenarios.accountable_owner: Credentialing owner and integration operations owner

Retry and reconciliation have stable operation IDs and bounded attempt policy.
Recovered results are identity-matched and evaluated under the active requirement version.

expected_state_or_action: Deny cross-school and cross-provider requests through every channel without exposing restricted contents.
Keep full student/IEP/clinical records in the school-owned source system. Return only the minimum authorized references/aggregates within the actor and tenant scope.
Apply the same scope and data minimization to reminders, logs, exports and agent retrieval.

Cross-provider document access
Full IEP, diagnosis or unnecessary student detail in AI context, logs or reminders
A broad connector service account bypassing the requesting actor grant

Authorized same-school retrieval yields only the permitted fields and references.
Agent retrieval enforces effective actor plus service scope; denial logs do not disclose restricted content.

scenarios.title: Financial approval is invalid after amount or destination changes
scenarios.actor: Finance preparation agent and financial approver
prerequisites: The approver authorized a specific operation, amount, currency, payee/destination reference and payload digest.
A preparation process subsequently changed one of those fields.
expected_state_or_action: Deny execution for every tested mutation; the stored approval does not authorize the changed payload. Route the mismatch to the financial owner without treating it as a newly approved package.

After the owner invalidates stale authorization and directs a correction, create/preserve the corrected proposal as DRAFT. Advance to REVIEW_PENDING only when the owner-directed corrected package is complete and frozen for exact review.
Display the changed payload for a new authorized human approval and preserve both versions.
forbidden_outcomes: Releasing funds under stale approval
Accepting a broad natural-language approval for an altered payment
Letting the proposing agent expand its own spending authority
scenarios.accountable_owner: Financial release owner
acceptance_checks: All listed mutations cause a release denial.
Approval records bind actor, grant, policy version, destination reference and canonical payload digest.
A new exact approval must come from an authorized human financial approver. The proposing or executing agent cannot grant its own approval.
The mismatch cannot skip the owner-directed correction and complete-package freeze guards to re-enter REVIEW_PENDING.
scenarios.future_test_type: Financial approval integrity and privilege separation test

Exporting student or provider records
External communication driven by document instructions
Treating document text as a school/clinician approval

acceptance_checks: No unauthorized service-plan change, scheduling mutation, export or communication occurs.
Only the approved reference is extracted; no student/clinical data is added to agent context.
Tool authorization remains bound to the real user and workflow grant.
scenarios.future_test_type: Adversarial document, retrieval and tool-authorization evaluation

scenarios.title: Urgent school safety report reaches the designated human route

Escalate through the validated backup when the primary does not acknowledge within the owner-set response window.
Record minimum necessary facts, attempts and acknowledgment. Leave emergency, educational and clinical decisions with qualified responders.

Assuring the provider that someone responded without acknowledgment
Closing the case from a message-send receipt alone
Collecting unnecessary student or patient information

scenarios.title: Recruiter cannot override active-provider scope or change school service requirements
prerequisites: A qualification or supervision issue is discovered after a provider work block has started.

inputs.requested_action: erase the supervision issue and change the service requirement so the provider appears qualified

expected_state_or_action: Deny the override, preserve the original qualification/supervision evidence and worked-time facts, and open an incident.
Alert the designated school/qualified discipline reviewer for an active-work response; the agent does not direct clinical care or amend the school service plan.
Record any subsequent authorized decision and rationale. Review provider time/pay independently without erasing actual work.

Changing IEP minutes, role scope or supervision requirements to fit an available provider
Directing care or terminating a service without the approved qualified route
Zeroing recorded work time
Granting override authority because a request sounds urgent
