acceptance_checks: The unauthorized request is denied and audited.
Original work and school-owned service references remain intact; any corrections are versioned by their authorized owners.
The active issue has a qualified school route and separate time/pay review.
scenarios.future_test_type: Privilege escalation, active-assignment incident and audit-history test

scenarios.title: Screening authorization and disputed consumer-report findings follow their own review path
scenarios.actor: Screening preparation agent and designated employment reviewer
prerequisites: The proposed screening workflow uses a third-party consumer report only after the launch applicability and required authorization/notice process have been selected and approved by the accountable reviewer.
Ordinary consent to share a provider profile with a school is recorded, but separate screening authorization is initially missing.
The fixture has two stages: authorization gating, then a simulated flagged/disputed result after the required authorization is actually recorded. No real screening order or report exists.

inputs.provider_dispute: the reported match is not me

expected_state_or_action: Deny the screening order while its specific authorization is missing; profile-sharing consent must not substitute for screening authorization.
After valid authorization, preserve any returned flag and provider dispute as restricted evidence, and route to the named employment reviewer.

The agent may prepare the approved review/notice workflow, but no automatic rejection, adverse decision or consequential notice is sent without the required owner decision and exact content approval. Readiness stays unresolved until the reviewed requirements are met.
forbidden_outcomes: Ordering a consumer report from generic school-submission consent
Automatic rejection or discipline from a vendor flag
Treating a disputed match as established identity
Sharing the full screening report with ordinary school scheduling users
Skipping or inventing applicability-specific notice and dispute steps
scenarios.accountable_owner: Employment review owner and screening/privacy owner
acceptance_checks: Stage one produces no vendor screening order and records the authorization gap.
Stage two retains authorization version, vendor result reference, dispute and restricted access history.
A flagged/disputed result creates an owned review case, without a final adverse employment decision.
The chosen applicability-specific notice/decision gates and exact human approval are visible before any consequential communication.
scenarios.future_test_type: Screening authorization, adverse-action review workflow and restricted-report access integration test

scenarios.title: Conflicting district documentation thresholds and deadlines stay unresolved until assigned
scenarios.actor: Contract/rule extraction and billing preparation agents
prerequisites: Two school-contract evidence excerpts contain conflicting documentation thresholds and deadlines, and their correct district/version applicability has not yet been resolved.
The numbers below are deliberately conflicting synthetic rule examples. They are not presented as universal or chosen contract terms.
Payroll has its own independently classified worked-time evidence.
expected_state_or_action: Retain both source excerpts, extracted values, version claims and scope uncertainty; do not choose a rule by string order, apparent strictness or a global default.

Keep the invoice DRAFT and open a contract/billing-owner resolution case for the correct district, contract version, threshold meaning, calendar and triggering event. It cannot become a frozen REVIEW_PENDING issue package until the applicable rules, billing quantities and due basis are approved.
After an authorized resolution, apply the selected scoped rule version prospectively to the relevant invoice evidence and retain the rationale. Continue independently authorized payroll handling.
forbidden_outcomes: Automatically choosing 95% or 100% without scope resolution
Combining a threshold from one district with a deadline from another
Treating business days and calendar days as equivalent
Applying a universal billing threshold to all school customers
Automatically withholding provider pay because invoice-rule applicability is unresolved
scenarios.accountable_owner: Contract/rule owner and school billing owner; separate payroll owner
acceptance_checks: The conflicting values remain separately traceable to their input evidence.
No invoice readiness or issuance occurs before district/version and deadline semantics are resolved.
The owner resolution records rule version, scope and rationale; re-evaluation uses that exact version.
The rule conflict does not automatically mutate pay hours, pay amount or payroll authorization.
scenarios.future_test_type: Rule provenance, district/version scoping and invoice approval integration test

sources.published_or_effective: Issued 2026-06-23; bids due 2026-07-06. Award and option exercise not established.
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 64 pages. Read alongside LC05 amendment and LC06 incorporated guidance.
sources.directly_observed_fact: The procurement covers leave replacement for OT/PT/SLP and excludes assistants. It specifies authorized orders, district documentation systems, school-day billing limits, nonbillable closures, documented service thresholds, missed-service plans and monthly electronic invoicing. Documentation thresholds and deadline wording differ across sections.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: District-specific IFB, not recovered Amergis operations. Several clauses use OT/PT-specific wording inside a broader related-services procurement. Resolve scope and conflicting text before implementation.

sources.title: DCPS GAGA-2026-I-0191 Amendment 001, questions and answers
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 4 pages.
sources.directly_observed_fact: DCPS seeks one vendor offering all requested disciplines. Virtual-only bids may be considered, with in-person preferred; virtual delivery must use DCPS's platform. Virtual staff retain specified attendance and screening requirements. Additional fees beyond the proposed hourly rate are excluded.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: This amendment modifies one procurement. It contradicts any assumption that a vendor can always use its own teletherapy platform or waive onsite-style screening for remote providers.

sources.title: DCPS Missed Related Services and Untimely Assessment Guidelines
sources.published_or_effective: Cover April 2017; page footers March 2017. Referenced and attached to the June 2026 procurement.
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 16 pages; official 2026 procurement links this document.
sources.directly_observed_fact: Guidance distinguishes provider absence, student absence/unavailability and school closure. Service and make-up records include reasons, durations, attempts and related communications. It uses legacy SEDS terminology, while the 2026 solicitation uses PSSP.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Do not apply a 2017 district procedure universally or translate its system names mechanically. District/clinician decisions about individual impact and remediation remain necessary.

sources.title: ASHA school services FAQ: caseload, workload, service delivery and work setting
sources.section_or_page: Questions: Does ASHA have a recommendation for caseload size?; policy on making up missed sessions?; one service delivery model versus another?
sources.retrieval: Fresh primary association webpage retrieval succeeded.
sources.directly_observed_fact: ASHA does not set a universal minimum/maximum caseload or a missed-session policy. It emphasizes total workload and individualized district consideration of missed-service impact. It does not prescribe a single service-delivery model.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Professional association guidance, not a substitute for selected-jurisdiction law, adopted district policy or a clinician's assessment.

sources.title: Amergis Educational Staffing Teletherapy Platform
sources.section_or_page: Security and accessibility; Clinically valid evaluations; Frequently Asked Questions
sources.directly_observed_fact: Amergis advertises room links without student accounts/downloads, waiting rooms, therapy-minute tracking, session-activity reporting and technical support. It also claims no stored student session data.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Marketing capabilities and compliance claims are not independently verified architecture, APIs, permissions or certifications. Reporting versus no-storage scope remains unresolved. Do not infer licensed assessment reuse rights.

sources.title: Amergis school SLP posting, Willard Missouri, position 1179375
sources.directly_observed_fact: This posting requires active assignment-state SLP licensure, describes CCC-SLP as preferred or state/contract dependent, and makes several health credentials conditional. It describes evaluation and documentation duties and employment-status-dependent benefits.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: One supplier job description, not authoritative Missouri law, a guaranteed vacancy, actual compensation or universal SLP qualification policy. URL job number and displayed position ID differ; retain both.

sources.title: IDEA §300.34 — Related services
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved
sources.supports: Speech-language pathology, occupational therapy and physical therapy are identified related services. OT and PT are services supplied by qualified practitioners; discipline-specific functions differ.
sources.limit: Does not establish the qualifications or scope for a selected state, school or individual.

sources.title: IDEA §300.156(b) — Related services personnel and paraprofessionals
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed subsection text retrieved; parent section direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: Qualifications must align with applicable state-recognized discipline requirements. Related-services requirements cannot be waived on an emergency, temporary or provisional basis. Appropriately trained and supervised assistants may assist in accordance with state law, regulation or written policy.
sources.limit: Does not make a national association credential, professional license and school credential interchangeable.

sources.title: IDEA §300.320(a) — IEP content
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed subsection text retrieved; parent section direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: An IEP includes goals, progress measurement/reporting, services and projected start, frequency, location and duration.
sources.limit: Provides no universal therapy minutes or caseload. The individual authorized plan supplies service obligations.

sources.title: IDEA §300.323(d) — IEP access and implementation responsibilities
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official subsection and official CFR text retrieved through search; parent section direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: Responsible providers must have access to the IEP and be informed of their implementation responsibilities and required accommodations, modifications and supports.
sources.limit: Does not prescribe a vendor's data model or make a schedule equivalent to delivered service.

sources.title: FERPA regulations — 34 CFR Part 99
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, Student Privacy Policy Office
sources.evidence_status: Official full page retrieved
sources.supports: Covered schools need consent or an applicable disclosure exception. Outsourced school officials require an institutional function, school control, permitted use/redisclosure and legitimate educational interest. Parents and eligible students have access/amendment rights; pending inspection requests restrict destruction.
sources.limit: A staffing contract alone does not establish the exception; schools and record types differ. Technical logging proposed here is broader than any universal FERPA disclosure-log requirement.

sources.title: FERPA or HIPAA for school student health records held by an outside provider
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.evidence_status: Official full page retrieved
sources.supports: Student health records maintained by a provider acting for a FERPA-covered school are education records under FERPA, rather than HIPAA records. A provider acting independently requires a different analysis, including HIPAA covered-entity status.
sources.limit: Record purpose and relationship determine the regime; school location alone does not. This does not establish a blanket BAA requirement.

sources.title: Background Checks: What Employers Need to Know
sources.publisher: Federal Trade Commission and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
sources.evidence_status: Official full page retrieved
sources.supports: Employment consumer reports require standalone disclosure and written authorization. Adverse-action processing includes pre-decision report/rights information and a subsequent notice. Equal-treatment, medical-inquiry and record-disposal requirements also apply as specified.
sources.limit: School fingerprinting, clearance, registries, employment-law coverage and state/local restrictions need separate research. The source does not establish a universal waiting interval.

sources.title: DOL Fact Sheet #22 — Hours Worked under the FLSA
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved; canonical direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: Compensable time can extend beyond scheduled work and include permitted work. Meal, training, waiting and travel treatment depend on the facts.
sources.limit: Employment status, exemption, overtime rules and state requirements remain unresolved; not every therapist or activity has the same pay treatment.

sources.title: DOL Fact Sheet #21 — FLSA recordkeeping
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved; direct fetch of indexed language URL returned 403
sources.supports: Covered employers maintain accurate employee, daily/weekly time and wage records. The federal baseline described includes three years for payroll records and two years for wage-computation supporting records.
sources.limit: These periods are not a universal retention schedule for student, credential, personnel or litigation records.

sources.title: IDEA §300.624 — Destruction of information
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education
sources.evidence_status: Official indexed text retrieved; direct fetch returned 403
sources.supports: The public agency informs parents when IDEA Part B personal information is no longer needed for educational services; parental destruction requests then apply, with a specified permanent-record exception.
sources.limit: School counsel must reconcile the applicable duties, holds and record categories; vendor contract termination is not itself the complete retention rule.

sources.fact: External applications use OAuth registration, service-account configuration and explicitly assigned endpoint permissions. Instance version and authorized metadata must be obtained.
sources.limitation: Generic vendor documentation; does not establish Amergis deployment or our access.

sources.title: Certiphi ATS Toolbox

sources.limitation: Marketing capability evidence only; current schema, package, pricing and test access remain unverified.

sources.limitation: Professional guidance; not an enacted universal caseload or compensation rule.

independent_review.title: Independent review of school therapy requirements research
independent_review.status: Pass for research and proposed bounded specification; no unresolved review findings
independent_review.scope: Evidence-linked requirements for schools and therapists, using SLP as a planning example with OT/PT and assistant distinctions. Review does not establish production readiness or jurisdiction-specific compliance.

checks.evidence: Discovery scope uses schools and therapists; SLP is expressly a worked example. OBR01/02 and the discipline checklist separate SLP/SLPA, OT/OTA and PT/PTA requirements; state and district remain open.

LC01/02 identify expired initial terms and unverified renewals; LC03/04/05 identify district solicitations rather than awarded Amergis contracts or nationwide rules. Vendor capabilities are not asserted as tested integrations.

Independently opened Bristol solicitation and DCPS solicitation. Downloaded DCPS amendment with validated system TLS after web-tool open failed. Confirmed district-specific modality, conflicting documentation thresholds/deadlines and named district systems. HHS school-record FAQ and indexed IDEA personnel rule support the stated conditionality.
J05/J06, OBR03/05/06 and VR09 keep clinical delivery, IEP eligibility/goals/minutes, attestations and missed-service remedies with qualified people and the authorized school process.

Initial scope keeps clinical/IEP content in district-designated systems. OBR07/08/09 require disclosure authority, purpose/assignment scope and relationship-based FERPA/HIPAA classification. Opaque references are explicitly still potentially protected data.

LCR06, OBR12, VR04 and J07 distinguish worked time, delivered service and customer billing; invoice rejection does not silently suppress payroll review. J08 and VR06 require exact-payload financial approval.

checks.topic: Draft field presence and transition prerequisites
checks.evidence: Required-at-create lists now govern initial presence; consent and submission approval evidence are nullable/deferred until required by the relevant transition. ASHA workload reference resolves to integrations V05.

Missing identity or fresh verification remains INCOMPLETE; interval expiry produces EXPIRED plus assignment HOLD; unresolved assistant scope is not a qualified rejection. Billing-rule conflict stays DRAFT. Stale financial approval follows owner-directed correction/re-freeze. All scenario state labels resolve.

All 43 requirement source references and journey/object/scenario links resolve. Eight requirements have textual acceptance criteria but no dedicated scenario; linked scenarios are explicitly partial. The bounded domain excludes multi-session/multi-school routing, assistant placement, clinical records and teletherapy delivery.

Ran check_scenarios.py on 26 scenario specifications, four Decimal financial fixtures and eight unmeasured metrics. It passed fixture shape, references, arithmetic, interval and group-duration consistency. The checker explicitly reports that no product acceptance tests, vendor conformance or live validation were performed.
Root corrected compact field/command decoding and structured validation text rendering. This is source/DOM-level review; no rendered browser or live application behavior is established.

checks.topic: Domain structure, ownership and command semantics
checks.evidence: Independent domain reviewer confirmed all nine declared state graphs are reachable, each nonterminal can reach a terminal, and 50 transition commands join uniquely. Reviewed authoritative records, credential/worksite scope, permissions, exact/current approvals, atomic reservations and idempotency. Cross-file reviewer re-read the corrected readiness, time/payroll, reconfirmation and command-envelope fields. This validates the proposed design structure only.

findings.issue: Legacy RN domain and scenarios contradicted the selected schools/therapists market.
findings.resolution: Replaced with school-therapy scope, SLP example, OT/PT distinctions, district-authorized modality and explicit bounded work-block design.

findings.issue: Initial required-field declarations demanded signed consent and recruiter approval before legitimate DRAFT records could exist.
findings.resolution: Added per-object required_at_create rules and deferred/nullable evidence with transition-specific prerequisites.

findings.issue: Domain ASHA workload reference incorrectly pointed to V07 (CMS).
findings.resolution: Corrected to phase5 integrations source V05.

findings.issue: Several expected scenario states skipped domain guards or used a different expiry meaning.
findings.resolution: SC05/07/19 now preserve INCOMPLETE; SC06 uses EXPIRED; SC26 stays DRAFT until billing rules resolve; SC21 describes owner-controlled correction and re-freezing without a premature state assertion.

findings.issue: SC21 allowed a policy exception for financial agent self-approval contrary to the pilot authority model.
findings.resolution: Removed the exception; exact new approval requires an authorized human financial approver.

findings.issue: Report builder expected expanded field dictionaries and rendered structured validation text as a string.
findings.resolution: Root added compact-format decoding and structured rendering.

findings.issue: Payroll batch review needs an unambiguous state after a time revision is exported; PAY_READY corrections need a safe superseding path.
findings.resolution: DS-C30 accepts PAY_READY or EXPORTED lines uniquely allocated to the same batch; DS-C29 allows owner-controlled void/supersession of unallocated PAY_READY revisions while transferring all work claims. Exported/issued corrections remain linked adjustments.

findings.issue: Runtime command UUID and DS-Cxx command-definition identifier need distinct fields.
findings.resolution: Runtime command_id remains a UUID; command_type identifies one registered DS-Cxx transition or declared non-transition operation. All operations use the audited envelope.

findings.issue: Reconfirmation from HOLD must reacquire fenced worker and slot reservations atomically.
findings.resolution: DS-C20 requires atomic reacquisition/validation of worker and slot locks with fencing before reconfirmation from HOLD.

findings.issue: Dispatch must explicitly check approval expiry, revocation, current approver authority and effective policy.
findings.resolution: The dispatch envelope requires current, unrevoked approval and currently authorized approver under the applicable policy; exact version/payload binding remains mandatory.

findings.issue: Worksite-specific readiness needs a required explicit worksite reference and exact assignment match; shared district policy alone is insufficient.
findings.resolution: DS-O06 now requires same-tenant/client worksite_id, explicitly matching the assignment school, in addition to worker, policy and interval.

limitations: No selected state, district, employment model, executed customer contract or operating vendor agreement has been validated.
No interviews, live student data, authenticated portals, vendor writes or product acceptance execution occurred in this review.
Public source spot checks are selective; they do not establish completeness of all legal, procurement or clinical requirements.
The domain model is a bounded staffing coordination design, not a full IEP, clinical delivery, multi-school scheduling or reimbursement specification.

Eight dedicated scenario-design gaps remain explicitly tracked: LCR03, LCR14, OBR04, OBR09, OBR13, VR02, VR11 and VR14. Existing linked scenarios do not establish exhaustive requirement or transition coverage.
No measured automation benefit, security effectiveness, legal completeness, profitability or product readiness follows from schema, graph or arithmetic consistency.
